newsitem.title: VIETNAM: U.S. admiral discusses defence with Vietnam's PM.
newsitem.headline: U.S. admiral discusses defence with Vietnam's PM.

text.p: Visiting U.S. Admiral Joseph Prueher was due to meet Vietnam's Prime Minister, Vo Van Kiet, on Friday to discuss defence ties between the two former enemies, a U.S. military official said.

Prueher, U.S. Commander-in-chief for the Pacific, arrived in Vietnam on Thursday on a tour aimed at assessing progress in efforts to resolve the fate of the 2,128 U.S. servicemen still listed as missing in action from the war in Indochina.

A public affairs spokeswoman for the U.S. Joint Task Force Full Accounting office in Hanoi said Prueher on Thursday visited a B-52 bomber crash site outside the Vietnamese capital where excavation work has been in progress since last year.
His schedule also includes talks with officials at the Ministry of Defence.
"He's here to observe first hand the operations of the joint task force. But it's basically a visit about initiating contacts," she said.

Prueher is the first senior U.S. military official to visit since Washington normalised diplomatic relations with Hanoi and opened an embassy in the Vietnamese capital in 1995, 20 years after the end of the Vietnam war.
Washington does not yet have an ambassador to Vietnam, but the Senate Confirmation process to appoint former representative Douglas "Pete" Peterson to the post has been under way for several weeks.
